sentences.text: Philosophy of religion examines religious beliefs, practices, experiences, and forms of life using philosophical argument.
The field includes questions about gods, ultimate reality, liberation, ritual, revelation, and religious language.
It should not assume that every tradition centers on belief in a single creator God.

Ontological arguments associated with Anselm reason from the concept of God; cosmological arguments appeal to dependence or causation; and design arguments appeal to features of order or apparent purpose.

sentences.text: Questions about divine foreknowledge, eternity, providence, and human freedom introduce further tensions.
Augustine, al-Ghazālī, Thomas Aquinas, and Søren Kierkegaard represent contrasting approaches to faith and philosophical reasoning.

sentences.text: Indian traditions have developed sustained arguments about self, ultimate reality, causation, testimony, and liberation.
Nyāya thinkers defend philosophical arguments concerning a supreme being, while Buddhist traditions generally reject a permanent creator and examine suffering and dependent origination.

sentences.text: These are not simply alternative answers to questions posed in Christian theology.
Confucian reflections on Heaven, ritual, and cultivation and Daoist discussions of the Dao raise philosophical questions that do not always fit the category of a personal deity.
Philosophical analysis of religious traditions also considers sacred practices, cosmology, and community, rather than reducing religion to propositions about supernatural beings.
Religious statements may function as metaphysical assertions, moral commitments, symbolic narratives, or expressions within practices.
Wittgenstein-inspired approaches explore the place of such language in forms of life.
Philosophers disagree over mystical experience, pluralism, and whether divergent traditions can make compatible truth claims.
Questions about religious authority, conscience, secular institutions, freedom of religion, and interreligious justice connect philosophy of religion with ethics and politics.
Contemporary inquiry also considers gender, colonial histories, ecology, and how religious communities interpret and revise their traditions.
Philosophy of religion examines religious traditions and wider questions of religious meaning: what religion is, what God might be, and what significance the cosmos and history might have.
